column1: truculence§The truculence of his reply surprised a committee that had asked a perfectly ordinary question.§他回复中的**凶蛮**让一个只问了个再普通不过的问题的委员会大吃一惊。§truc（凶残）
trustworthy§The most trustworthy source in the file is a caretaker's logbook that nobody thought to open for nine years.§卷宗里最**可信的**来源是一本看管人的值班簿，九年无人想到打开它。§
tryst§The tryst was recorded in four letters, and the letters are the only reason we know either name.§这次**幽会**记在四封信里，而这些信是我们知道两个名字的唯一原因。§
tumultuous§The tumultuous meeting ran four hours over and produced a decision nobody could later explain.§这场**喧闹混乱的**会议超时四小时，产生了一个后来谁也解释不清的决定。§tumult（骚动）
turmoil§The turmoil lasted nine months, and the four people who kept the office running were never mentioned.§这场**动荡**持续九个月，而维持办公室运转的四个人从未被提及。§
turpitude§The charge of moral turpitude was dropped in 1974 and follows him, in four reference books, still.§这项**道德败坏**的指控在 1974 年被撤销，却仍出现在四本工具书里。§turp（丑恶）
tyrannical§The tyrannical head of department was, according to nine former students, also the best teacher they had.§这位**专横的**系主任，据九位从前的学生说，也是他们遇到过的最好的老师。§tyrann（僭主）
tyranny§The tyranny of the deadline produced four rushed decisions and one that turned out to be brilliant.§期限的**暴政**催生了四个仓促决定，其中一个后来证明极其高明。§
tyrant§The tyrant kept detailed records, which is why we know the names of nine thousand people he exiled.§这位**暴君**留下详细记录，所以我们知道他流放的九千人的名字。§
ubiquitous§The device was exotic in 1998 and ubiquitous by 2004, and four industries disappeared in between.§这种设备在 1998 年还稀罕，到 2004 年已**无处不在**，其间四个行业消失了。§ubi（哪里）
unacquainted§The reviewer was plainly unacquainted with four decades of work on exactly this question.§这位评审显然**不熟悉**恰恰针对这个问题的四十年研究。§
unadorned§The unadorned account is more damning than any accusation: nine dates and four sums of money.§这份**不加修饰的**陈述比任何指控都更具杀伤力——九个日期和四笔款项。§un（不）+ adorn（装饰）
unaffected§Her manner was unaffected in a room where everyone else had prepared a version of themselves.§在一个人人都准备好一个版本的自己的房间里，她的举止是**不做作的**。§
unalterable§The deadline was described as unalterable and was, in the end, altered four times.§这个期限被称作**不可更改的**，最终被改了四次。§un（不）+ alter（改变）
unanticipated§The unanticipated consequence turned out to be the useful one: four small schools started sharing a single teacher.§**未曾预料的**后果反倒是有用的那个——四所小学校开始共用一位教师。§
unappreciated§The largely unappreciated work of nine technicians is what made four separate prize-winning papers possible at all.§九位技师**基本未受赏识的**工作，才使得四篇获奖论文成为可能。§
unapproachable§The director was unapproachable for four years and, after one crisis, answered every email himself.§这位主任**难以接近**了四年，一场危机之后开始亲自回复每一封邮件。§
unassuming§The unassuming man in the corner had written the standard textbook the other nine were quoting.§角落里那位**不事张扬的**先生，正是另外九人所引用的标准教科书的作者。§un（不）+ assume（自负）
unattainable§The target was unattainable and everybody knew it, and four managers signed up to it anyway.§这个指标**无法达成**且人人心知肚明，四位经理还是签了字。§
unattractive§The unattractive option was the only workable one, and it took nine months to be chosen.§那个**没有吸引力的**选项是唯一可行的，花了九个月才被选中。§
unavoidable§The delay itself was unavoidable, and the four months of official silence surrounding it certainly were not.§延误本身是**不可避免的**，而围绕它的四个月官方沉默显然不是。§
unaware§He was unaware of the rule for nine years, and so, it turned out, was everyone enforcing it.§他九年**不知道**这条规则，而结果执行它的人也都不知道。§
unbounded§Her enthusiasm was unbounded and her budget was four hundred pounds, which shaped the project.§她的热情是**无限的**而预算是四百英镑，这塑造了整个项目。§
uncensored§The uncensored edition appeared in 1994 and differs from the first in about nine hundred words.§**未删节的**版本在 1994 年问世，与初版相差约九百字。§
unchanged§The wording is unchanged since 1911, and four courts have now read it four different ways.§这段措辞自 1911 年起**未曾改动**，如今四家法院读出了四种意思。§
unchanging§The unchanging part of the job is the part nobody applies for: nine hours of the same four checks.§这份工作**一成不变的**部分正是没人来应聘的部分——九小时同样的四项检查。§
unconcerned§He seemed entirely unconcerned about the figures until somebody quietly converted them into staff hours.§他对这些数字似乎**毫不在意**，直到有人悄悄把它们换算成人力工时。§
unconditional§The offer was unconditional in the letter and, in the four appendices, considerably less so.§这份录取在信里是**无条件的**，在四份附录里则远非如此。§
unconscionable§The nine-month wait for a decision that takes four minutes is unconscionable, and the report says so.§为一个四分钟就能做出的决定等九个月是**不合情理的**，报告这么说了。§un（不）+ conscion ← conscience（良心）
undaunted§Undaunted by four rejections, she sent the manuscript to a ninth publisher and it sold immediately.§四次退稿也**未使她气馁**，她把稿子寄给第九家出版社，立刻就卖出去了。§un（不）+ daunt（威吓）
underscore§The four resignations underscore a problem that nine surveys had already described in detail.§这四起辞职**凸显**了一个九次调查早已详细描述过的问题。§under（下面）+ score（划线）
undesirable§The undesirable outcome was also the most likely one, and the plan assumed it would not happen.§这个**不受欢迎的**结果同时也是最可能的，而计划假定它不会发生。§
unequivocal§The instruction was unequivocal, and four people still managed to read it in two different ways.§这条指令**毫不含糊**，而四个人仍然读出了两种意思。§un（不）+ equi（相等）+ voc（声音，同 voice 声音）
uneven§The quality is uneven: four of the nine chapters are excellent and the rest were clearly rushed.§质量**参差不齐**——九章里有四章极佳，其余显然是赶出来的。§
unexpectedness§The unexpectedness of the result is what made four laboratories check it before publishing.§这个结果的**出人意料**，正是四家实验室在发表前先复核它的原因。§
unflappable§The unflappable chair let a nine-minute argument run and then settled it in about four sentences.§这位**处变不惊的**主席让一场九分钟的争论跑完，然后用约四句话摆平了它。§un（不）+ flap（慌乱扑腾）
unforeseen§The unforeseen cost was four hundred thousand pounds, and nine similar projects had all reported it.§这笔**未预见到的**成本是四十万英镑，而九个类似项目都报告过它。§
ungainly§The ungainly machine works better than the four elegant ones that were designed to replace it.§这台**笨拙难看的**机器，比为取代它而设计的四台优雅机器都好用。§un（不）+ gainly（合宜的）
unhinge§Nine months of night shifts unhinged a man who had been, by every account, entirely steady.§九个月的夜班让一个所有人都说极稳当的人**精神错乱**。§un（去掉）+ hinge（合页）→ 门脱了轴
uniformity§The uniformity of the answers suggested collusion, and four minutes of checking confirmed it.§这些答案的**一致**暗示了串通，四分钟的核对就证实了。§uni（单一）+ form（形状）
unintelligible§The instructions were unintelligible to nine of the ten people asked to follow them.§这些说明对被要求遵照执行的十人中的九人来说**难以理解**。§un（不）+ intelligible（可理解的）
unique§The specimen is unique: no second example has been found in four hundred years of searching.§这件标本是**独一无二的**——四百年搜寻未发现第二件。§uni（单一）
unjust§The rule is not merely inconvenient but unjust, and nine years of appeals have said so.§这条规则不只是不便，而是**不公正的**，九年的上诉一直这么说。§un（不）+ just（公正）
unleash§One broadcast unleashed four thousand complaints about a practice that had run for nine years.§一次播出**释放**出四千条对一项已存在九年的做法的投诉。§un（解开）+ leash（皮带）
unlikely§The unlikely explanation turned out to be right, and the four likely ones were all checked first.§那个**不大可能的**解释结果是对的，而四个可能的解释都先被查过了。§
unlimited§The access was described as unlimited and turned out to mean four hours a week.§这项权限被描述为**无限的**，结果意思是每周四小时。§
unmediated§The unmediated recording is nine hours long and contradicts the four-page summary in nine places.§**未经中介处理的**录音有九小时长，在九处与那份四页摘要矛盾。§
unnatural§The pose looks unnatural because it is: the sitter held it for four separate three-hour sessions.§这个姿势看着**不自然**是有道理的——模特分四次、每次三小时保持着它。§
unnecessary§Nine of the eleven forms are unnecessary, and the two that matter were introduced in 1994.§十一张表里有九张是**不必要的**，要紧的两张是 1994 年引入的。§
unobtainable§The part is unobtainable, and the machine it belongs to still runs nine hours a day.§这个零件**已无处可得**，而它所属的机器仍在每天运转九小时。§
unorthodox§Her unorthodox method was rejected for four years and is now the standard first step.§她**非正统的**方法被否定四年，如今是标准的第一步。§un（不）+ orthodox（正统的）
unpalatable§The unpalatable fact is on page nine: four of the schemes have never been evaluated at all.§**令人难以接受的**事实在第九页——四个方案从未被评估过。§un（不）+ palate（味觉）
unparalleled§The collection is unparalleled in Europe and, for nine months of every year, entirely inaccessible to the public.§这批藏品在欧洲**无与伦比**，而每年有九个月公众完全无法接触。§un（不）+ parallel（平行／匹敌）
unpopular§The unpopular decision was correct, and the four people who made it all lost their jobs.§这个**不得人心的**决定是正确的，而做出它的四个人都丢了工作。§
unprecedented§The step was unprecedented and, once taken, was repeated nine times in the following four years.§这一步是**史无前例的**，一旦迈出，此后四年就被重复了九次。§un（不）+ precedent（先例）
unpredictable§The supply is unpredictable, and nine of the eleven bakeries here now mill their own flour.§供应**难以预测**，如今这里十一家面包房中有九家自己磨面粉。§
unpretentious§The unpretentious little restaurant on the corner has four tables, no sign, and a nine-month waiting list.§街角这家**不事张扬的**小餐馆有四张桌子、没有招牌，还有九个月的等位名单。§
unprincipled§The unprincipled thing was not the deal but the memo written afterwards to justify it.§**没有原则的**不是那笔交易，而是事后为其辩解的那份备忘录。§
unproductive§The four-hour meeting was entirely unproductive, and the nine-minute corridor conversation afterwards settled everything.§那场四小时的会议**毫无成果**，而随后九分钟的走廊交谈把一切都定了。§
unqualified§The appointment was unqualified in both senses: he had no training, and nobody attached any conditions.§这次任命在两种意义上都是**没有资格限定的**——他没受过训练，也没人附加任何条件。§
unrealistic§The timetable was unrealistic and the team met it, at a cost the report describes in four paragraphs.§这个时间表**不切实际**而团队做到了，代价在报告里用四段描述。§
unrealized§The unrealized plan of 1908 is more famous than the four buildings that were actually built.§1908 年那个**未实现的**方案，比实际建成的四栋楼更有名。§
unrelenting§The unrelenting pace lasted nine weeks, and four of the eleven staff did not return afterwards.§这种**毫不放松的**节奏持续九周，十一名员工中有四人此后没再回来。§un（不）+ relent（软化）
unruly§The unruly public meeting produced the four best suggestions the council received all year.§这场**难以控制的**公开会议，产出了议会全年收到的最好的四条建议。§un（不）+ rule（规则）
unscrupulous§The unscrupulous agent charged nine hundred pounds for a form that costs four to file.§这个**毫无顾忌的**中介为一张办理费四英镑的表格收了九百英镑。§un（不）+ scruple（顾忌）
unseen§The unseen cost is the one the report never mentions: nine hundred hours of unpaid overtime.§**看不见的**成本是报告从未提及的那项——九百小时的无偿加班。§
unsettle§The question visibly unsettled a witness who had answered nine much harder ones without hesitating at all.§这个问题明显**扰乱**了一位曾毫不迟疑回答过九个难得多的问题的证人。§un（去掉）+ settle（安定）
unstable§The compound is unstable above four degrees, and the shipment spent nine hours on a warm platform.§这种化合物在四度以上**不稳定**，而这批货在温暖的站台上放了九小时。§
